missed.maker: NXP Semiconductors (JLCPCB API 'NXP Semicon'); S1 NXP
missed.why: P2 did not consider the TJA144x family. The TJA1443 is NXP's pin-compatible successor to the TJA1043, which P2 dropped for 240 ns and for giving no normal-to-standby time. Figures from TJA1443 Rev. 2, 15 October 2021 (https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/data-sheet/TJA1443.pdf, read 2026-09-28T17:56:21Z). STB_N (pin 14) is an active-LOW standby input with a 20 to 80 kOhm pull-down, so the enable node drives it directly with no inverter (V18). With EN held high, STB_N low is the go-to-sleep command: Sleep follows after th(gotosleep), 24 to 50 us, and the transmitter is disabled in Standby and in Sleep. A rising edge on STB_N leaves Sleep, and the part then enters Normal with STB_N and EN high (section 7.1.1.5). tt(moch), the mode change transition time, is 50 us max (V19: 5 ms). VCANH -36 to +40 V (V24: +30 V). CAN FD up to 5 Mbit/s (V21). td(TXDL-RXDL) and td(TXDH-RXDH) 215 ns max (limit 237 ns). VIO 2.95 to 5.5 V; VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V; VBAT 4.5 to 28 V. No I_off is given for STB_N, so it takes the 4.7 kOhm series resistor. With that resistor and the minimum 20 kOhm pull-down, a 3.3 V enable node gives 2.67 V at the pin, above VIH 0.7 x VIO = 2.31 V. Constraints: SOIC-14 with VBAT, EN, INH, ERR_N and WAKE to wire. VBAT from the 5 V rail holds only while that rail stays at 4.5 V or above, and that rail's tolerance is open (V100). Stock: JLCPCB 403, presale 402, expand, 0.7162 USD at 10 (vendors.py jlcpcb C3233835, 2026-09-28T17:54:24Z). Digi-Key TJA1443AT/0Z: 7016, Active, lead 16 weeks (18:01:52Z). NXP family page https://www.nxp.com/products/TJA144x: 'Status - Active' (18:03:11Z); the page lists TJA1443AT. The part page https://www.nxp.com/part/TJA1443AT carries no status in its body (18:02:44Z).

Meets the link's values (TJA1443 Rev. 2, read 2026-09-28T17:56:21Z): VIO 2.95 to 5.5 V; -36 to +40 V (V25: 5.5 V); 215 ns (limit 350 ns). JLCPCB 403 (17:54:24Z). Digi-Key 7016, Active (18:01:52Z). NXP TJA144x Active (18:03:11Z). The same constraints apply as in the external entry: SOIC-14, VBAT, EN.

missed.why: P2 did not consider this family. The Infineon CAN FD transceivers P2 could have taken instead are all not for new design: TLE9251VSJ, TLE9351VSJ, TLE9350VSJ, TLE9250VSJ and TLE7251VLE at 17:57:39Z to 17:58:02Z (datalayer-productStatusInfo on https://www.infineon.com/part/<name>). The TLE9252VSK page reads 'active and preferred' (17:58:02Z). Datasheet TLE9252V Rev. 1.11, 2019-10-17 (https://www.infineon.com/assets/row/public/documents/10/49/infineon-tle9252v-datasheet-en.pdf, read 2026-09-28T17:58:40Z). NSTB is an active-low standby input. With EN held high, NSTB low is the Go-to-Sleep command, which disables the transmitter, then Sleep. A rising edge on NSTB returns the part to Normal (section 6.5.2) (V18). tMode 20 us max (V19). VCANH -40 to +40 V (V24). 5 Mbit/s (V21). tLoop 215 ns max (limit 237 ns). VIO 3.0 to 5.5 V; VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V. Constraints the re-rank must weigh: (1) VBAT is specified from 5.5 to 40 V, with VBAT_UV 4.8 to 5.5 V. The 5 V rail cannot supply VBAT; it needs the board's 6.0 to 20 V input path, which is outside P2's 'supply from the board's rails' requirement as P2 wrote it. (2) NSTB has no I_off. IMODE_H is 20 to 220 uA at VMODE = VIO. If that current is resistive, 4.7 kOhm leaves 2.51 V against VMODE_H 0.7 x VIO = 2.31 V. If it is constant at 220 uA, the pin sees 2.27 V, under 2.31 V. The datasheet does not say which. Stock: JLCPCB C540122 196, presale 196, expand, 1.4437 USD at 10 (2026-09-28T17:58:19Z); C191266 TLE9252VSKXUMA1 0 (17:58:20Z). exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Ranks below the five: Digi-Key 0 (17:26:00Z); its only alternate route is SN65HVD232DR, whose pins 5 and 8 are NC where the '230 has Vref and Rs, and whether NC pin 8 may be tied to ground is not stated; narrowest bus rating.
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The SN65HVD232DR is not its only alternate route. The SN65HVD231DR (C129257) is in the same datasheet, SLOS346O (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn65hvd230.pdf, read 2026-09-28T18:04:47Z). It has the '230's pins: Vref output on pin 5 and Rs on pin 8. It has the same t(LOOP1), 115 ns max, and t(LOOP2), 135 ns max, at V(Rs) = 0 V. It differs only in what Rs high selects: sleep, driver and receiver off, against the '230's standby. A circuit with Rs at 0 V does not use that mode. The device table gives the SN65HVD231 -40 to 85 °C, which covers the board's 0 to 50 °C (V7). JLCPCB C129257: stockCount 9366, presale 9172, 1.1693 USD at 10 (vendors.py jlcpcb, 2026-09-28T17:54:20Z), which passes rules 1 to 4. It is therefore a rule-5 alternate in the same circuit. Digi-Key SN65HVD231DR: 0, Active (18:04:59Z), and SN65HVD230DR still 0 (18:02:11Z). The other statements in the reason hold.
